column3: According to the Azure SQL Database documentation, the database-per-tenant pattern uses a multitenant application with many databases, all of them single-tenant databases, and provisions a new database for each new tenant.
The application tier is scaled up vertically or out horizontally based on the workload, independently of the number or scale of the individual databases.

According to the same documentation, the alternative is to store many tenants in a multitenant database, whose schema must have one or more tenant identifier columns so that the data of any given tenant can be retrieved selectively.
In that pattern, static code and reference data is stored only once and shared by all tenants.
